name: Sentence Start Variety (Opener Diversity)
description: Examines the taxonomic diversity of words and grammatical structures used at the beginning of sentences. AI models heavily favor safe, standard subject-verb syntaxes, often starting consecutive sentences with definite articles ('The'), basic pronouns ('It', 'We', 'They'), or formulaic transitional adverbs ('Additionally', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover'). Human writers naturally employ a much richer assortment of sentence openers, frequently beginning with prepositional phrases, dependent clauses, gerunds, or coordinating conjunctions to create dynamic pacing and narrative flow.
algorithm: Syntax-Tree Opener Classification and N-Gram Distribution
mechanism: The algorithm extracts the first 1-3 words of every sentence and tags their Part-of-Speech. It calculates the 'Opener Entropy' by measuring how evenly distributed the different types of starting structures are. If a text has 20 sentences and 15 of them start with 'The' or a pronoun, the entropy score is severely low, indicating artificial generation. The system also flags the presence of AI-specific transitional boilerplate ('In conclusion,', 'Ultimately,', 'First and foremost,') used at the head of paragraphs.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing essays, articles, and long-form emails where the repetitive, droning cadence of AI sentence generation becomes statistically obvious.
strengths:
• Extremely fast and computationally lightweight compared to deep neural analysis.
• Excellent at catching AI text that has been lightly edited in the middle of sentences but left untouched at the boundaries.
limitations:
• Short texts (under 10 sentences) do not provide a large enough sample size to calculate meaningful opener variance.
• Deliberately simplistic human writing (like children's books or basic instructional guides) may flag as AI due to naturally low sentence start variety.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging of Sentence-Initial Tokens
Metric: Opener POS Entropy and Transitional Boilerplate Frequency
Output: 0-100 Opener Rigidity (Artificial Cadence) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 68-76% accuracy. Serves best as a complementary feature within a broader Syntactic Complexity analysis suite.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.
